selection: Fixed seed 787103; diagnostic sentiment/framing strata followed by fixed-seed fill; exact 40-ID manifest frozen before review; sample is not prevalence-weighted or a representative accuracy estimate
error_types: VADER: positive vocabulary such as agree, protect, safety, curiosity and profit can dominate adverse AI-risk context
VADER: scientific problem solved is penalized by stumped; job-prospect declines can score near neutral
Negation scope: not intelligent enough; not perfect but useful; double negatives
Quotation/attribution/satire: risk statement quoted, disputed or mocked is not endorsement
Framing undercoverage: paraphrased scientific advances, declining job prospects, harms/control language not matching fixed phrases
Framing false positives: opportunity to repair harm; social-information bubble rather than valuation bubble; capex alone does not establish financial risk
Stance false positives: experts can refer to workshop attendees; lexical negation scope can reject the wrong proposition
Long X posts mix AI commentary with company criticism, PR insults, politics and unrelated emotion/financial vocabulary
one_correction: One correction: recognize orthographic/entity variants of existing control/safety concepts (out-of-control, A.I. safety/alignment, rogue agents). No sentiment tuning; other contextual errors remain limitations.
conclusion: Diagnostic agreement is limited. Preserve the generic VADER measure as text sentiment in AI-related material; do not describe it as a validated AI-specific attitude or investment-sentiment measure. Rule shares describe explicit dictionary matches, not comprehensive true risk-framing prevalence.
